title: Texas high-school softball full-authority pilot research docket — NOT PUBLISHED
dataPolicy: Verified 2026–27 UIL softball district identities and clearly season-labelled 2025–26 historical team evidence. Research-only. No individual pages auto-published or approved by this file.
method: Exact match school name+conference+district+region to official UIL softball PDF. Primary school/UIL records for historical facts. Unresolved areas stay in gaps and must be closed for complete-first-publication acceptance. Current staff cannot be inferred from prior championship rosters. Expanded with primary-source historical UIL finals, official school schedule/current-season caveats, school staff spelling corroboration and known stale postseason notices on October 11, 2026. Every historical claim remains season-labelled and neither roster reprints nor inferred playing-field addresses are approved. October 11 independent primary-source award pass: 2026 UIL TGCA all-tournament groups for four champions, 2025 Shiner/Ganado honors, 2025 Katy district venue naming and official 2026 Ganado calendar venue naming. Venue recognition DOES NOT imply exact field parcel, admission, ADA, parking or current 2027 location. Third-party Amarillo team records explicitly not elevated to official school confirmations. October 11 coach role research: current school athletic websites identify named Shiner, Pearland and Katy softball head coaches as-of verification (not explicit Spring 2027 appointments), Ganado official faculty listings confirm James Harp employment but do not imply current role, and Amarillo school live feed confirms actual softball launch activity without reliable program foundation year. October 11 independent TEA/NCES physical campus crosswalk: Katy HS campus is in Fort Bend County (despite Katy ISD district association with Harris County), Shiner HS is a combined grades 7–12 campus and TEA vs NCES student counts are not identical, and Ganado, Pearland, Amarillo Highland Park each have exact state campus IDs and dated non-UIL enrollments. No student private data collected. Substantive October 11 Amarillo-specific original reportage pass identified contemporaneous May 18, 2024 construction/coach interviews, $6m anticipated fields portion of a $130m bond plan, inaugural head coach Eliza Martinez, historical 2024-25 assistant Mary Lieberknecht from third-party archived schedule and Spring 2025 real game fixture results. All year/venue claims retain evidence level; no implication 2027 coach or 2024 plan's as-built field details. October 11 separate Amarillo-specific May 17, 2024 KFDA/KCBD original news source confirmed historic planned softball complex south of existing football field; distinct hpisd.org Dallas 2024 bond and TDLR softball project are unrelated and excluded. Historical venue renaming found October 11: Katy ISD board video July 27 2026 item 9.11 and independent August 6 press document honoring former coach Kalum Haack by naming Katy High's softball field. Prior 2025 schedule's KHS-Softball Field label is pre-naming, not necessarily the current official visitor-facing name. This change was researched BEFORE first authority page publication. October 11 verified Kalum Haack college coaching history directly against University of Kansas Athletics published 1988–95 year-by-year coach/records. These are college facts for biography, not Katy high school state titles; omit Alabama 1997–98 specific counts pending media-guide visual verification. October 12 official district verification: 2025 ribbon cutting for completed baseball/softball fields, 'HP Softball Field' named as youth camp location, school-issued first district win over Follett; source checks retain original actual 2026-10-11 dates when not rechecked and 2026-10-12 for new posts. College coach archival span 1988–1995 corrected from erroneous 1991–95 placeholder. October 12 Pearland original 2023 district-hosted girls softball camp flyer verifies historical school softball venue name 'PHS Lady Oiler Softball Complex' and 2023 coaching roles, but contains confusing/incorrect state-title list and private return-mail address. This historical flyer does not verify the field's 2027 name/entrance, and is not a substitute for UIL archival championship finals. October 12 original UIL pre-2012 history: Shiner 2007 championship runner-up (Bosqueville 4–1), 2008 champion (Bosqueville 11–1), 2011 tournament head coach Brandon Siegel with assistants, and dated tournament record-book categories. No student roster copied.

facts.claim: The 2026–27 UIL softball alignment lists Shiner in 2A District 29, Region IV, alongside Ganado, Flatonia, Danbury, Burton, Louise, Weimar and Moulton.
Shiner won the 2026 UIL 2A Division II championship; the championship archive names Shiner as champion.
The official 2025–26 state-team record names Jason Keller as head coach and lists Anastacia Rehak, Patrick Walker and Kailey Moeller as assistants.
The Shiner official 2025–26 state-team profile lists fifteen state-tournament appearances from 1996 through 2026, including championships marked in prior years.

Shiner ISD's 2026 softball PDF published home-and-away opponents, varsity and JV distinctions, practices/scrimmages and a school contact line; it is a historical 2026 schedule, not proof of a released spring 2027 schedule.
The 2026 title game against Sundown finished 5–2; a contemporaneous recap describes Shiner avenging its narrow 2025 championship defeat.
The official UIL 2025–26 state-team page displays a 31–7 record in its tournament entry; do not silently substitute a third-party 22–7 subset or call it the verified postfinal record.

UIL's 2025–26 Shiner state-team sheet identifies championship years 2001, 2002, 2008, 2011, 2015, 2016, 2024 and 2026 within 15 state-tournament appearances; the 2001 and 2002 title-game results have separate historical UIL final records.

UIL's historical 2001 softball championship archive records Shiner defeating Joaquin 2–0 in the 1A title game after a 2–1 semifinal over Brock, with extra-inning details preserved in the official bracket.
UIL's historical 2002 softball championship record shows Shiner winning the 1A championship over Bosqueville 11–1 in five innings after defeating Collinsville 10–0 in a five-inning semifinal.

UIL's Shiner 2016–17 state-team sheet identifies Steven Cerny as the coach with assistants John Hoelter and Ray Neal; these are verified historic staff roles, distinct from Jason Keller's 2025–26 tenure.
The UIL 2025 2A Division II final bracket identifies Sundown's 9–3 championship victory over Shiner on May 29, 2025, making Shiner a runner-up that season rather than the champion.

The UIL May 24, 2026 state-tournament pairings listed Shiner at 31–7 entering its Thursday May 28 final against Sundown; this shows the record's pre-title-game cutoff date, not a verified postfinal total.

UIL's all-time softball tournament archive confirms Shiner had 15 state-tournament appearances and eight championships through 2026, despite crossing 1A, 2A, and 2A-Division-II eras; records must retain their historical conference rather than retroactively assigning all titles to modern 2A.

The UIL May 31, 2026 all-tournament release credits Shiner with five 2A Division II honorees, including its championship game MVP Lauren Springfield; tournament awards are not interchangeable with full-season all-district or statewide TGCA awards.

UIL's 2025 all-tournament release records Shiner honorees even though Sundown defeated Shiner in the 2025 2A-DII title game; those distinctions belong to the 2025 season and must not be mislabelled as a team championship.

A Shiner local sports archive from the 2001–02 school year identifies David Goetz as Lady Comanches head coach, with Paula Lester as assistant, and reports an historic winning streak; corroborate with an original school/UIL coaching record before treating all ancillary streak totals as verified.

The Shiner ISD athletics softball page currently names Jason Keller with Anastacia Rehak, Patrick Walker and Kailey Moeller in its Lady Comanche program coaching group, consistent with the 2025–26 UIL tournament submission; this is a present website listing checked October 11, 2026, not a dated 2027 appointment letter.

TEA campus 143903001 identifies Shiner High School in Lavaca County as a 7th–12th grade campus with 309 students in its 2025 School Report Card sourced to 2024–25. This is not 309 high-school varsity athletes or the special UIL alignment enrollment. NCES shows 311 enrollment using its different count definition.

The original UIL 2007 Class 1A championship bracket shows Shiner defeating McLeod 3–0 in its semifinal before finishing state runner-up to Bosqueville in a 4–1 final. The UIL's listed 21–6–1 for Shiner was a pre-tournament submission and must not be presented as a final-season record.

The official 2008 UIL 1A state championship bracket documents Shiner beating Maud 11–1 in its semifinal and then Bosqueville 11–1 in the state final. These are specific 2008 scores and opponent identities, not proof that the 2007 runner-up season ended with a championship.

The original UIL 2010–11 Shiner softball state team submission names Brandon Siegel as head coach with John Hoelter and Steven Cerny assisting; Shiner's community 2008 archival snapshot also identifies Brandon Siegel as head coach that season. This supports a documented early-coaching era before Steven Cerny later became head coach and before Jason Keller, without assigning coach credit to uncited seasons.

The UIL softball record book includes Shiner team tournament offensive benchmarks in 2010–11 and 2015–16, including 13 team RBI against Lindsay in a 2011 tournament game and 23 team RBI across the 2016 tournament. Record-book categories and whole-tournament versus single-game scopes must stay distinct, not be rewritten as season-long school records.

facts.claim: Ganado and Shiner are separate UIL 2A District 29 softball schools in the 2026–27 official alignment; Ganado is not in Shiner's football alignment by default.
Ganado won the 2025 and 2026 UIL 2A Division I softball titles; the UIL source lists 2025 and 2026 tournament appearances.
The 2025 Texas House enrolled resolution reports Ganado's first softball state championship, its unbeaten postseason and 5–4 final against Riesel.
The 2026 championship game against Bosqueville ended 5–2, the second state title in a row according to contemporaneous coverage.

UIL's 2025–26 team record identifies coach James Harp and assistant coaches Malina Andel, Matt Ervin and Shauna Hazlewood; treat these as 2026-season staff until a current 2027 directory confirms continuity.
UIL's 2025–26 state-team entry displays 33–2–1, a tournament-sheet record that should not be called a definitive after-final record without dated reconciliation.

Ganado ISD's schedules directory explicitly provides a 2025–26 Ganado softball schedule, while its other athletics listings distinguish baseball, football, track, basketball and volleyball; the dated 2026 softball source is historical, not the unreleased 2027 calendar.
The UIL May 24, 2026 championship pairings list Ganado at 33–2–1 against Bosqueville at 30–8–1 entering the 2A Division I final; the 33–2–1 record is a prefinal submitted tally.

Ganado High School's school-controlled 2025–26 athletics calendar explicitly schedules varsity softball senior night and JV home games at the named Ganado Softball Field, establishing a real school-used field identity, but not a street address or verified accessibility/entrance details.

The UIL May 31, 2026 softball all-tournament awards list five Ganado 2A Division I selections, led by MVP Saylor Bures; these are season-specific honors selected by the Texas Girls Coaches Association.
The UIL June 1, 2025 all-tournament list identifies Ganado's Kyla Stancik as 2025 2A-DI title-game MVP; this is a different season and honoree than Ganado's 2026 Saylor Bures MVP.

Ganado High's current faculty directory includes James Harp and Shauna Hazlewood as faculty and Joshua Ervin as athletics director. The 2025–26 UIL softball state-team sheet separately identifies James Harp as head coach and Shauna Hazlewood as an assistant, but the newer directory does not independently label either person as a 2027 softball coach.

Ganado ISD identifies Ganado High School at 501 West Devers and the separate district administration at 210 South 6th Street; neither address is source-labelled the varsity girls softball playing field, so use the campus address for school identity only.

Ganado ISD's own facility map page links stadium, high school gym and junior high gym facilities but provides no separately labelled softball field map or visitor entrance. The school event calendar verifies Ganado Softball Field's name without revealing an address.

TEA campus 120902001 is Ganado High School in Jackson County, 9th–12th grades, with 221 students in its 2025 school report card. Ganado ISD separately confirms the actual school campus at 501 West Devers; do not substitute the district headquarters at 210 South Sixth Street or presume it is the varsity softball field.

facts.claim: UIL's 2026–27 softball conference table lists Katy High School in Conference 6A, District 22, Region III, with eight other Katy-named campuses as district peers.
Katy High School won the 2026 UIL 6A Division II state title, defeating Forney 7–2 in the championship game.
Katy ISD's published post-championship recap reports the finished 2026 season at 39–5, with a 22-game winning streak and a reported 97th home run.
The older UIL tournament team submission lists 38–5 before the championship and enumerates four state appearances (2007, 2015, 2019, 2026); annotate the submission date when comparing records.
Katy ISD identifies 2015, 2019 and 2026 as its three 6A championship seasons.

The UIL 2025–26 state-team profile identifies head coach Meghan Brown VanEtta and assistants Brian Schmitt and Judy Whillock; Katy High's school directory carries the coach's current staff role under a different display spelling.

Katy High School's official campus athletic contact page gives 6331 Highway Blvd, Katy TX 77494 as its general campus address; this is not, by itself, evidence for the precise softball home-field entrance or spectator parking.

Katy's 2025–26 UIL submitted team sheet lists the Tigers' state appearances as 2007, 2015, 2019 and 2026, with title markers on 2015 and 2019; Katy ISD's June 1 report confirms 2026 as their third state championship.

The official February 7, 2025 Katy ISD athletics schedule calls Katy High's varsity softball venue 'KHS-Softball Field' and assigns multiple February 13–15 Katy home games there; this proves the named home venue in 2025, not a 2027 field policy or precise spectator entrance.

UIL's May 31, 2026 awards release lists six Katy softball selections to the Conference 6A Division II state all-tournament team, including championship-game MVP Haley Schmitt; the list is historical 2026 recognition, not a future team roster.

The Katy High School current athletics coaches directory identifies softball coach Megan Vanetta, while the separate faculty listing gives Megan Vanetta with a 'Science / Softball Head Coach' title. UIL's 2025–26 tournament sheet spells the previous season's head coach Meghan Brown VanEtta. Current school display spelling has priority for a present-tense school role, with the UIL archival form preserved only where discussing 2025–26.

Katy High's athletics directory identifies Judy Whillock as assistant athletic coordinator; the 2025–26 UIL tournament sheet lists her among softball assistants, but those are separately defined roles and do not alone establish her spring 2027 varsity-softball appointment.

Katy High School's exact Texas campus code is 101914001, and NCES records the physical 6331 Highway Boulevard school location in Fort Bend County with 3,543 students in 2024–25. Katy ISD has a Harris County district designation in some TEA reports, but that is not the Katy High campus county and must never be applied to its team page.

Katy ISD's official July 27, 2026 board meeting archive lists agenda item 9.11 as consideration of naming a portion of Katy High School. Contemporary August 6 local reporting states trustees unanimously APPROVED naming the high school's SOFTBALL FIELD in honor of retired longtime head coach Kalum Haack. This postdates historical athletic event calendars that simply call it 'KHS-Softball Field'; exact permanent sign wording and field visitor entrance remain unverified.

The field honoree Kalum Haack led Katy High's softball program for 26 years, including its 2015 and 2019 state championship seasons, and retired in May 2024, according to Katy-Fulshear Times' August 2026 board-vote account. Katy ISD separately inducted coach Kalum Haack and the school's 2015 state-champion softball team into its 2025 Athletics Hall of Honor, independently corroborating his lasting team legacy.

The detailed August 2026 Katy-Fulshear Times board-naming report credits retired coach Kalum Haack with more than 850 career wins at Katy High, two state titles in 2015 and 2019, 18 regional semifinal appearances and nine consecutive outright district championships at the end of his tenure. These are attributed historical reporter-compiled totals, not independently audited UIL career stats; seek the school athletics Hall of Honor citation or archival season-by-season evidence before presenting exact aggregate totals as official.

The University of Kansas official softball year-by-year archive independently confirms Kalum Haack was the Jayhawks' head coach every season from 1988 through 1995, including 45–10 in 1992, 31–15–1 in 1993 and 37–20 in 1994; this is documented college coaching history before his move to Alabama and his later 26-year Katy High dynasty, not a record of Katy High seasons.

The Kansas official softball archives place Gayle Luedke, not Kalum Haack, as the 1996 Jayhawks head coach; therefore press language saying he coached Kansas '1988–1995' must not be extended into an unsupported Kansas 1996 season when mapping his move toward Alabama's inaugural varsity softball program.

facts.claim: UIL lists Amarillo Highland Park in 2026–27 softball Conference 2A, District 1, Region I; listed peers include Gruver, Sanford-Fritch, Stinnett West Texas, Sunray, Booker and Follett.
The official Highland Park ISD website uses the Hornet identity and identifies its administrative address as 15300 Amarillo Blvd East, Amarillo TX 79108.

This Amarillo school is entirely separate from Dallas's Highland Park Scots, which compete under a different district and have their own coaches and stadium. Dallas softball program sources must be excluded from this team's research.
A third-party softball scoreboard provides a 2025–26 Amarillo Highland Park 9–16 record; this is a discovery lead and NOT a verified school-issued season total.

A third-party 2025–26 Amarillo Hornets softball snapshot identifies staff only as 'E. Martinez' (head coach) and 'M. Lieberknecht' (assistant), but first names and current appointments are not established by a Highland Park ISD primary source; neither can be published as verified 2026–27 staff.

The 2025–26 Amarillo Highland Park third-party season page records two April 23 playoff losses to Floydada, 0–16 and 1–17, but those scores must be checked against official UIL brackets or school athletics reports before inclusion as fully verified varsity program milestones.

The real Amarillo Highland Park ISD's archived live feed promotes merchandise for its 'two newest programs,' softball and baseball, and records an early softball parent meeting, offering genuine district evidence that the softball program had a comparatively recent school launch; the relative 'almost two years ago' feed labels are insufficient to claim a precise inaugural season or first varsity game.

Amarillo Highland Park High School is TEA campus 188903001 in Potter County, grades 9–12, with 213 students shown in the 2025 TEA campus comparison report. The matching NCES physical location is 15300 Amarillo Boulevard East and cannot be substituted with the entirely different Dallas Highland Park campus or unrelated softball facility.

Independent Amarillo-area reporter Kale Steed documented Highland Park ISD's May 2024 groundbreaking for new baseball and softball complexes under a previously approved $130 million school bond package, reporting approximately $6 million budgeted for those facilities; this is a 2024 construction plan and not proof the final project cost or visitor amenities.

On May 18, 2024, Press Pass Sports quoted Superintendent Jimmy Hannon and Athletic Director Ty Stout describing how student requests and school-board support led Amarillo Highland Park to introduce its first baseball and softball programs, targeting first competition in spring 2025. A separately archived 2024–25 Lady Hornets game schedule corroborates actual first-year softball planning and historical opponents.

Eliza Martinez, a former Plains High School track and powerlifting coach and Slaton graduate, was named Amarillo Highland Park's inaugural head SOFTBALL coach in April 2024, according to the original contemporaneous May 18, 2024 Press Pass Sports report. The 2024–25 Lady Hornets schedule independently labels Eliza Martinez as head coach and Mary Lieberknecht as assistant; neither document establishes confirmed staffing for spring 2027.

The 2024–25 Lady Hornets softball schedule explicitly contains home scrimmages against Dalhart and Littlefield, varsity games against River Road, Sunray and other UIL opponents, and a home Sanford-Fritch senior night scheduled April 15. This is season-specific archived fixture evidence; scheduled dates and times are not conclusive proof a game occurred or of a final score.

The spring 2025 Amarillo Highland Park versus Sanford-Fritch public scoreboard shows a completed March 22, 2025 varsity softball game, independent corroboration that the new program was playing games by spring 2025. This third-party game record does not itself verify the newly built stadium's completion, exact playing venue parcel or field-accessibility rules.

In its May 2024 construction coverage, Press Pass Sports quotes the Highland Park superintendent that both planned softball and baseball diamonds were intended to have artificial-turf playing fields and lighting; those announced construction specifications must be checked against later district as-built photographs and bond records before described as confirmed 2026–27 facilities.

An independent May 17, 2024 KFDA news report states Amarillo Highland Park ISD's planned baseball and softball complex was at the SOUTH END OF THE EXISTING FOOTBALL FIELD, with the anticipated first season in spring 2025. This is a historically sourced campus-area orientation only; it does not verify the final softball playing field's named gate, street entrance or compliant accessible spectator route.

Amarillo Highland Park ISD announced a Friday, March 28, 2025 ribbon cutting at 4 p.m. for its new softball and baseball fields, with the Sod Poodles mascot scheduled for a ceremonial first pitch. This official district announcement upgrades the old 2024 construction plan to evidence that new playing fields were being inaugurated in March 2025; it does not verify a public parking map, ADA spectator route, exact street-facing field entrance or completed inspection.

A June 2025 Highland Park ISD camp announcement specifically locates its inaugural youth softball camp at 'HP Softball Field', providing an official historical name for the Amarillo Hornets softball venue. The district calendar distinguishes the sport from baseball; the name alone is not confirmation of 2027 season use, signage or visitor accessibility.

Amarillo Highland Park ISD's spring 2025 athletic news reports its varsity Lady Hornets earned a first district softball victory with a 15–2 win over Follett. This is a school-issued historical program milestone, not the full inaugural season final record or proof that a specific spectator entrance served that game.
